name: CH32V003J4M6
title: CH32V003 RISC-V microcontroller, 48 MHz, 16 KB flash, 2 KB SRAM
summary: The CH32V003 family is a 32-bit RISC-V (RV32EC) microcontroller running at up to 48 MHz from a 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply, with 16 KB flash, 2 KB SRAM and a factory bootloader. It carries a 7-channel DMA, a 10-bit ADC, an op-amp/comparator, an advanced-control and a general-purpose 16-bit timer, two watchdogs, USART, I2C and SPI, and debugs over a single wire. It comes in TSSOP20, QFN20, SOP16 and SOP8, rated -40 ℃ to 85 ℃; the SOP8 CH32V003J4M6 brings out 6 I/O and has no SPI.
key_figures: 2.7 V to 5.5 V (2.8 V min with ADC)
6.4 mA typ, 48 MHz on HSI, all peripherals on, 3.3 V
10-bit, up to 1.71 MS/s at 24 MHz clock

circuits.title: Supply and decoupling
circuits.description: A single 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply feeds VDD, with one 0.1 µF capacitor across VDD and VSS at the chip. The analog supply decoupling reference uses the same 0.1 µF across VDD and VSS.

circuits.title: External clock into OSC_IN
circuits.description: A clock source drives OSC_IN (PA1) directly at fHSE_ext, 4 MHz to 25 MHz; OSC_OUT (PA2) is left open.
notes: OSC_IN high level 0.8VDD to VDD, low level 0 to 0.2VDD, duty cycle 40 % to 60 %.

circuits.title: 24 MHz crystal on OSC_IN and OSC_OUT
circuits.description: A 24 MHz crystal sits between OSC_IN (PA1) and OSC_OUT (PA2), each end loaded to ground by its own capacitor, CL1 and CL2, of equal value.

parts.note: Sized to the load the crystal is specified for; CL1 = CL2.

notes: Recommended crystal load capacitance 20 pF with series impedance RS = 60 Ω.

circuits.title: External reset pin
circuits.description: A push-button pulls NRST (PD7) to ground for a manual reset, and a 0.1 µF capacitor connects NRST to ground. The pull-up to VDD (RPU, 35 kΩ to 55 kΩ) is inside the chip. The SOP8 part has no NRST pin.

circuits.title: ADC input connection
circuits.description: A signal source VAIN reaches an ADC input pin AINx through its source resistance RAIN; CP is the stray capacitance of the pad and board at that pin, about 5 pF. Inside, each input has clamp diodes to VDD and VSS (VT about 0.6 V) and samples onto CADC through RADC. RAIN is kept below the limit of the RAIN equation for the chosen sampling time.

parts.note: Source resistance, limited by the maximum RAIN equation.
Parasitic capacitance of the pad and board.

notes: AINx is any ADC input; PD4 (A7) stands for it.

operation.text: QingKe RISC-V2A core running the RV32EC instruction set, little-endian, supporting machine mode, at up to 48 MHz system clock. It carries the PFIC interrupt controller, a two-level hardware interrupt stack, custom extended instructions and the single-wire SDI debug port.

2 KB SRAM (lost at power-down), 16 KB code flash for program and constants, 1920 bytes of system flash holding the factory bootloader, 64 bytes of non-volatile system configuration and 64 bytes of user option bytes. Code can jump between the bootloader and the user program in either direction.

Code flash 0x0800 0000 to 0x0800 4000; system flash (bootloader) from 0x1FFF F000; vendor bytes 0x1FFF F7C0; option bytes 0x1FFF F800 to 0x1FFF F840; SRAM 0x2000 0000 to 0x2000 0800; peripherals from 0x4000 0000; core private peripherals from 0xE000 0000. Address 0 maps to either the code flash or the system flash, chosen by software.

VDD from 2.7 V to 5.5 V powers the I/O and the internal regulator; rated operation is at 3.3 V or 5 V. With the ADC in use, performance falls off below 2.9 V. The output high level of the I/O follows VDD.

A power-on / power-down reset circuit is always active and holds the chip in reset while VDD is under VPOR/PDR, so no external reset circuit is required. A programmable voltage detector, enabled in software, compares VDD with a threshold chosen by PLS[2:0] and can raise an interrupt on VDD falling or rising through it.
The internal regulator starts on at reset. In normal operation it supplies the core; it drops to a low-power state when the system enters Standby.
The CPU clock stops while peripheral clocks and peripherals keep running. Lightest saving, quickest wake-up (30 µs typ). It ends on any interrupt or wake-up event.

Entered with PDDS and SLEEPDEEP set and a WFI or WFE instruction. The core supply is cut and the HSI and HSE oscillators stop, giving the lowest current (7.6 µA to 9.4 µA typ). It ends on any EXTI line (any of the 18 I/O pins, the PVD output or the AWU auto-wakeup), a low level on NRST, or an IWDG reset; wake-up takes about 200 µs.

The PFIC handles up to 255 vectors; 4 core interrupts and 23 peripheral interrupts are used. It offers a non-maskable interrupt, hardware stacking with no instruction overhead, two vector-table-free fast interrupt channels (VTF), a vector table holding addresses or instructions, two-level nesting and tail chaining. Its registers are reachable in machine mode.

Eight edge detectors produce interrupt or event requests, each set for rising, falling or both edges and masked on its own, with a pending register. Any of the 18 GPIO pins can be routed to an external interrupt line. Pulses shorter than an internal AHB clock period are caught; the minimum detected width is 10 ns.

One general-purpose DMA controller with 7 channels moves data between memories, from peripherals to memory and from memory to peripherals with ring-buffer mode, serving the timers, ADC, USART, I2C and SPI. Priority, length, source and destination are set per channel; DMA and CPU share SRAM through an arbiter.

The 24 MHz factory-trimmed HSI RC runs the CPU after reset. An external 4 MHz to 25 MHz HSE (crystal or clock on OSC_IN) or the PLL, which doubles HSI or HSE, can be selected instead. The 128 kHz LSI clocks the independent watchdog and the auto-wakeup. HCLK is SYSCLK through an AHB prescaler of /1 to /256, 48 MHz max; the ADC clock is divided from it (/2 to /128) and MCO can output HSI, HSE or the PLL clock. With clock security enabled and HSE in use, a failed HSE switches the system to the HSI and turns off HSE and PLL; an interrupt can report it. After waking from low power the system runs on the internal RC.

10-bit ADC with up to 8 external channels and 2 internal channels, input range 0 to VDD. Per-channel sampling time; single, continuous, scan or discontinuous conversion; an analog watchdog on one or more channels; triggering from timers or external pins with an optional programmable trigger delay; DMA support. Board and pad capacitance at the input (about 5 pF) costs accuracy; lowering fADC recovers it.

16-bit up/down auto-reload counter with a 16-bit prescaler, able to drive three-phase PWM on 6 channels with complementary outputs, dead-time insertion, repetition counter and break input for motor control. It links with the other timer for synchronization.

16-bit up/down auto-reload counter with a 16-bit prescaler and 4 channels for input capture, output compare, PWM and one-pulse output; it also reads incremental encoders and 1 to 3 Hall sensors, has its own DMA request, and can be frozen in debug with PWM outputs disabled.

The independent watchdog counts down over 12 bits with 7 prescaler settings, clocked by the LSI, so it runs in Standby; it starts by software or by option byte. The window watchdog, clocked from the main clock, counts down over 7 bits with an early-warning interrupt. Both can be frozen in debug. The core's SysTick is a 32-bit counter with auto-reload and a selectable clock, exception number 15.

One USART: full-duplex asynchronous, synchronous one-way and single-wire half-duplex modes, LIN, ISO7816 smart card, IrDA SIR, CTS/RTS flow control, multiprocessor communication, fractional baud rate generator and DMA.

One SPI, master or slave with run-time switching and multi-master, full or half duplex, selectable CPOL and CPHA, 8- or 16-bit frames, hardware CRC, basic SD and MMC modes and DMA. The A4M6 and J4M6 parts have no SPI.
One I2C interface, multi-master or slave, standard and fast speeds, 7- or 10-bit addressing with two slave addresses in 7-bit mode, and a hardware CRC generator and checker.

Up to 18 GPIO in three ports (PA, PC, PD). Each pin is set by software as an open-drain or push-pull output, input (floating, pulled up or pulled down), or an alternate function. All pins except those with an analog function have high current capability. A lock mechanism freezes the I/O configuration. Each pin sources or sinks up to ±8 mA within the VOL/VOH limits and up to ±20 mA with relaxed levels; the total stays within the absolute maximum ratings.

One op-amp that can also work as a comparator, internally connectable to the ADC and to TIM2 CH1. Its inputs and output are chosen among several pins. It can amplify a small external signal into the ADC, or compare, sending the result to a GPIO or straight to a timer input.
One-wire serial debug interface on SWIO (PD1), active after power-up or reset. The HSI must be running while SDI is in use. On the SOP8 part SWIO shares pin 8 with PD4 and PD5.

Voltages are referred to VSS. Minimum and maximum figures hold over the worst case of temperature, supply and clock; typical figures are at 25 ℃ and VDD = 3.3 V or 5 V and are for guidance. Figures based on characterization, design or simulation are not production tested.

Supply current is measured in series with VDD at room temperature, VDD = 3.3 V or 5 V, all I/O as inputs with pull-down, HSI on when HSE is tested and HSE off when HSI is tested, HSE and HSI both 24 MHz, PLL (CLK×2) as system clock for 48 MHz and 16 MHz, and peripheral clocks on only for the all-peripherals figures. Current depends on supply, temperature, pin loading, clock, code location and code.
Package dimensions are in millimetres. Pin pitch is exact; every other dimension is within ±0.2 mm or ±10 %, whichever is larger.

CH32 V 003 J 4 M 6: V is a QingKe RISC-V general-purpose MCU; 0 is the value line (V2/V4 core, up to 48 MHz) and 03 the 16 KB basic general type with op-amp; the pin-count letter is J = 8, A = 16, F = 20; 4 is 16 KB flash; the package letter is M = SOP, P = TSSOP, U = QFN; 6 is -40 ℃ to 85 ℃.
